scope: Production CUDA Tile aligned16 structured-load opt-in, default / aligned request / default recheck; not standalone Driver probes.
methodology: Sequential default (native+Torch), aligned16 (native only), default recheck (native only). Seven raw graph-v2 samples per route retained, no filtering. Full packet/oracle revalidated. Ordinary source is byte-identical; alternate source only adds proven scalar alignment and exact load representation. Entry is a host prediction from final pointer residues, not a Driver trace. Recheck quantifies drift; this is not replicated randomized inference. No model fitting or precision changes.
protocol: 7 samples, 100ms target, 500ms warmup, graph batch100, 4 physical P cores mask0x15400
limitations: Host-predicted selected entry from actual final-pointer residues, not Driver execution trace.
Complete-operation graph throughput, not isolated kernel latency; Native preallocated outputs/hazard DAG differs from functional Torch allocation.
Sequential cohort order with default drift control; seven samples are retained, not a randomized independent experiment.
Structured memory is not universally profitable: scan regression retained; no operation-name exclusion, default change or model refit.
block=(1,1,1) is the Tile launch ABI, not a physical-thread/warp count.
Historical validated checkpoint performs full tensor/oracle checks; this projection rechecks only small receipts and scalar invariants.

source_receipts.revision_note: Captured HEAD plus uncommitted measured changes; exact compiler/runtime state identified by snapshot receipts, not HEAD alone.

semantics.graph_contract: Native: N complete identical workloads including every pipeline stage; same inputs/output/scratch allocations and hazard-DAG ordering. Independent pipeline stages may overlap across calls. R complete graph replays per timed sample, divided by N*R complete workloads; event-primed adaptive_replay_span_v2. Functional Torch output allocation is a separate contract.
